findings.title: Consort screening sum (Results 3.1 Participants, first sentence)
findings.description: Randomized plus excluded exceeds the screened total by 2. The exclusion reasons themselves reconcile exactly (30 + 24 = 54), and every subsequent stage of the flow reconciles exactly (122 - 3 = 119 treated; 119 - 9 = 110 FAS; 59 + 51 = 110; 21 + 19 = 40 and 38 + 32 = 70 summing to 110; 102 - 10 = 92 DTI; 92 - 11 = 81 rs-fMRI). So the discrepancy is isolated to the screening line: either 174 should read 176, or 2 patients are unaccounted for between screening and randomization. This was 1 inconsistent row out of 33 sums evaluated in a single batch.

Eight cells agree with their marking. This one does not: the lower-limb improvement over the treatment period T0-T1 is significant at the conventional 0.05 level under BOTH Welch (p = 0.0329) and Student (p = 0.0305) readings, yet carries no asterisk, while two cells with the asterisk have p = 0.0157 (dFMA-T T1-T2) and p = 0.0239 (dFMA-UL T1-T2). The unmarked significant difference favours PLACEBO (5.6 vs 3.3 points). The other six unmarked cells are comfortably non-significant (p = 0.12 to 0.75). No single threshold reproduces the printed pattern of asterisks: at alpha = 0.05 this cell should be starred, and at the Bonferroni-corrected threshold the paper says it used, the starred dFMA-UL T1-T2 cell (p = 0.0239) should not be. Note the paper does not state which test produced Table 2's markings beyond 'the independent t-test was used between the two groups to analyze the change in motor function'.

findings.title: Table1 lesion volume p (Table 1, Lesion volume row)
findings.description: The tool returned highly_suspicious; I have recorded it as suspicious because that verdict rests on an assumption I supplied rather than one the paper states. RIVETS tests the reported p against what an independent t-test on the printed means and SDs could yield. The paper never says which test produced Table 1's p-values, and lesion volume is severely right-skewed (SD is 1.5x the mean, on a quantity bounded below by zero), so a rank-based test is the natural choice and would legitimately give a different p. The gap is the largest of the three Table 1 misses: reported 0.117 against an achievable two-tailed ceiling of 0.0954. Worth a clarification of which test was used, not an accusation.

consequence.explanation: Supports the claim of no baseline imbalance in lesion volume; under a t-test reading the true p would be nearer 0.09, still non-significant but closer to the threshold given the 26 cm3 raw difference.

findings.title: Table1 nihss p (Table 1, NIHSS row)
findings.description: Downgraded from highly_suspicious as above. The two printed means are identical to one decimal, so a t-test on the printed values gives p = 1.0, and even the widest rounding of the underlying means cannot push p below 0.8935. Reported 0.882 sits just outside that, by 0.011. NIHSS is a bounded ordinal score commonly analysed with Mann-Whitney, which would give a different p entirely, so this is best read as a test-type question. Of the seven continuous Table 1 rows checked this way, four (MMSE, FMA-T, FMA-UL, FMA-LL) are fully consistent.

consequence.explanation: Both readings are far from significance; the baseline-balance claim for stroke severity is unaffected.

findings.title: Lesion volume normality cerebrolysin
findings.description: The paper asserts that ALL assessment values were normally distributed by Shapiro-Wilk. For lesion volume that assertion is hard to sustain: a normal distribution with mean 43.9 and SD 66.7 places 25.5% of its mass below zero, and a lesion volume cannot be negative. The tool correctly notes this does not violate a distribution-free bound and that a parametric test needs normality of the sampling distribution of the MEAN, not of the raw values -- so this is a question about the stated normality check, not a reporting error in itself. It matters here mainly because it bears on which test Table 1's lesion-volume p-value came from (see table1_lesion_volume_p).

findings.title: Table3 interhemispheric identical sds (Table 3, Interhemispheric connectivity row)
findings.description: The same SD, 0.151, appears three times in a single row at three-decimal precision: Cerebrolysin at T0, placebo at T0, and placebo at T2. These are two independent groups at two different timepoints. This is a weak signal on its own -- identical SDs across groups recur by chance and rulebook rule 8 says to report but not escalate them alone -- and it is recorded here for completeness rather than as an anomaly in its own right. The formal duplication check over all three tables found no identical (mean, SD) pairs at all (see tables_duplication_scan).

findings.title: Table3 rsfmri paired correlations
findings.description: This is the strongest positive result in the sweep. All eight rs-fMRI paired tests report exact p-values to four decimals alongside both timepoint means and SDs and a known n, which lets the hidden pre-post correlation be recovered. findings.description: statcheck recovered nothing, and this is a parser limitation rather than a fact about the paper.
